A National Institution at a Crossroads

David Jones, the world’s oldest continuously operating department store trading under its original name, faces an uncertain future beyond the upcoming Christmas season. After 188 years, the Australian retailer—known affectionately as 'DJs'—is grappling with shifting consumer habits, the rise of online shopping, and sustained economic pressures.

A History of Cultural Significance

Founded in 1838, the store became a centerpiece of Australian urban life, hosting historic events like the 1969 moon landing broadcast and visits from royalty. Beyond retail, it served as a site for rites of passage, from first suit fittings to wedding registries. Historically, it set the standard for high fashion, acting as a gateway for international couture and, later, a major platform for iconic Australian designers like Carla Zampatti and Akira Isogawa.
